entry.summary: Sometimes the biggest performance gains come not from making core operations faster, but from eliminating unnecessary work surrounding them. That is exactly what we discovered while optimizing documen
entry.content: Sometimes the biggest performance gains come not from making core operations faster, but from eliminating unnecessary work surrounding them. That is exactly what we discovered while optimizing document lookup in MongoDB Atlas Search and Vector Search. By removing redundant query planning and execution overhead, we made search queries up to 5x faster without changing the underlying search algorithms.

entry.title: Ducks in a Column | DuckDB
entry.summary: DuckDB is fast among other reasons because it stores data by column, so a query reads only the columns it names. This post covers DuckDB features that take advantage of that design choice: querying fi
entry.content: DuckDB is fast among other reasons because it stores data by column, so a query reads only the columns it names. This post covers DuckDB features that take advantage of that design choice: querying files in place, column-level SQL, aggregation shortcuts, window functions, ASOF joins, and writing well-organized Parquet.
